title: Every money figure on catalogue and topic is the author's estimate for an invented persona, with no 'estimate' label and no basis
expected: Each value figure says 'estimate by the playbook's author' with its one-line basis and is plausible for the person's case
got: Value tile '$500 per episode, for the persona', catalogue value and 'Worth $X ... for <persona>' with no basis; economics.basis is never parsed and caveat is parsed but rendered nowhere; vs Characters' own cases: baggage $500 vs Bev ~$207.75, eu261 $1,300 vs ~EUR 800, eitc $3,000 vs ~$3,449 (Aisha) / ~$7,892 (Bev)
suggested_acceptance: Every rendered value figure has an adjacent source label ('author's estimate' + basis, or 'measured on invented data'); a test asserts basis text is parsed and rendered for all consumer playbooks

title: Two 'worth' dollar figures on one topic page disagree with no explanation (Value tile vs 'Filed on the bench')
expected: One headline worth figure, or both labelled as different quantities (estimate per episode vs measured on an invented case)
got: 10 of 11 consumer chores show different numbers: baggage $500 vs $203, eu261 $1,300 vs $5,445, unclaimed $400 vs $1,016; only credit-report agrees
suggested_acceptance: On every consumer topic page the flow result and Value tile carry distinct labels naming their source, or a single reconciled figure is shown

title: Bench per-act weights are rendered as dollars 'Filed on the bench' and summed into the catalogue's 'found on the bench'
expected: Weighted exposure units are never shown as money; only recovered dollars are
got: eitc 'Filed on the bench $4,000' = 4 x $1,000 weight ('an exposure unit and not money recovered'); credit-report $1,000 = 8 x $125; data-broker $32 = 5 x $6.45 while its Value says $0
suggested_acceptance: Playbooks whose truth values are weights carry a flag; the flow shows 'N of N acts' instead of $ and totalsLine excludes them

title: 'N x faster' leaves out the person's own review time (computed but not rendered) and the onboarding conversation
expected: Time saved counts the person's review and setup, says the hand minutes are an estimate, and says it is one bench run
got: Shown 35-92x; with review 18-47x (baggage 63x->22x, travel 92x->32x); beforeAfterOf builds 'your review N min' but topic.tsx renders only band.ratio
suggested_acceptance: Topic shows athena minutes including your_time_s and the line 'your review N min'; ratio computed on (wall + review)

title: The topic hero tells an invented persona's story with nothing on the hero saying it is invented
expected: Hero says 'An example, invented for testing' before the story; the caveat is reachable
got: Judges in 18 of 22 pairs read the page as 'about someone else' (Boston vet tech, San Diego office manager); only the gallery caption says 'invented portal world'
suggested_acceptance: Hero shows an 'Example case (invented)' label above p.brief and a disclosure that renders playbook.caveat

title: Internal vocabulary on every chores screen: catalogue 4, topic 6-7, practice run 5 words
expected: No rubric-list word unexplained on screens a home user reads
got: Catalogue: benched, exceed the bar, bench, edge ('Best edge'); topic: persona, bench, trap, world, turn, brief (+claim in internal sense on 4 chores); showcase: rehearsal, world, card, turn, brief. Bev C5 fail 10/10, Walt C4 fail
suggested_acceptance: A copy test fails if any rubric jargon word renders on catalogue/topic/showcase for a home-audience chore without an inline gloss

title: First-round answer options are the playbook's invented brands, which no real person uses
expected: Options are generic ('Gmail / Outlook / Yahoo / something else') or the person's own apps
got: 19 of 22 cases use at least one other portal; options offered Postwren, Cardhollow, Tripcairn, Aerolark, Streamquill; asides in 13 pairs ('I had to pick around them', 'made me nervous I was doing it wrong')
suggested_acceptance: Portal questions offer common real providers plus 'other'; invented bench names never appear as options in a live adopt

title: Rules the playbook researched and sourced are labelled '(my guess)' in the brief, and so are facts the person typed
expected: Statutory facts show their source ('Montreal Art. 31: 21 days after delivery'); the person's own answers read as confirmed
got: 49 '(my guess)' lines across 22 briefs (21-day complaint, 3h/6h thresholds, 30 days, 7/10 years); reg-e-bev 'told the bank 3 October (my guess)' though she said it
suggested_acceptance: A new slot status 'from the rule' renders with its citation, not '(my guess)'; answers the person typed are confirmed

title: 'What do I get back and when' is never answered, even where the case makes it computable
expected: The brief states an estimate for this case with its basis and an expected wait
got: Aisha asked in all 10 pairs; no brief gave a figure or timeline; baggage brief promised 'an exact total, not an up to' and gave none; computable: eitc ~$3,449, eu261 2 x EUR 400, class $117
suggested_acceptance: Each brief has an 'Expected for you' line: amount or range from her facts, labelled estimate, plus typical response time

title: A dollar figure appears in the practice run only when the world was NOT shaped like the case, yet it is labelled 'shaped like your case'
expected: A $ figure from the unmodified persona world is labelled 'the example's case, not yours'
got: found_usd is set only when the shape edited no row and kept the date; shown in 8/22 pairs: eu261 $5,445 (family of four) vs ~EUR 800 for Aisha and Bev; subscription-bev $613.50 vs ~$426; unclaimed-bev $1,016.43 vs $940.75; class-aisha $158 vs $117
suggested_acceptance: When found_usd is non-null the label says 'on the example's invented case (not shaped to yours)'

title: The 'shaped' practice-run result gives a card count and 'answer key ... rows' that nobody can check
expected: A plain summary: the letters she would send, to whom, for how much, by when, and what she left alone and why
got: 14 of 22 pairs: 'N cards proposed, against M in the recorded run. Your case changed rows the answer key was written for'; Aisha C6 null 10/10; the turn Player exists but there is no summary
suggested_acceptance: Showcase renders a list of proposed acts (company, amount, rule, deadline) above the player

title: Judge lead 'Exceeds (n=1) on the page' refuted; the single-run sample is computed but shown nowhere
expected: Next to 'N x faster' the page says 'one run so far'
got: verdict.label/sentence/sample are unused in scenes/chores; judges saw numbers.json, not the UI
suggested_acceptance: n=1 shown beside the time and value figures

title: Lead 'topic page never says what she asks first' refuted: gate diamonds render it, but each reason is hover-only
expected: Each gate's reason is visible as text on touch devices
got: flow.tsx renders 'Athena asks you first <label>' per gate; the why is only a title attribute; Aisha is phone-first
suggested_acceptance: Gate reason rendered as visible text under the label

title: Back and close exist, but no plain 'you can stop at any point; nothing leaves without your yes' before starting
expected: One sentence on topic and studio head stating stop/undo and approval
got: Crumb 'All playbooks', 'Close', 'Leave anyway?' and post-approval 'nothing was sent' exist; Bev C2 fail 6/10, null 4/10
suggested_acceptance: Studio head carries the stop/approval sentence; L2 checks Bev can find it

title: Facts from the playbook's persona leak into questions and briefs
expected: Questions and briefs use only the person's facts once they have named their own
got: 'your son' to pregnant Aisha; 'which of your two partnerships' to Walt; 'Flights between Dublin and Lisbon' and '2 hour 10 minute' delay in Bev's travel brief; Gina brief 'two partnerships (my guess)'
suggested_acceptance: A check rejects briefs/questions naming persona-only entities (from playbook persona/promise) absent from the person's answers

title: The person's own questions go unanswered, and sensitive questions come without need or reason
expected: A typed question is answered before the next card; sensitive questions only when the case needs them, with a reason
got: eitc-bev 'why do you need where IRS letters arrive' and 'what does Form 8332 do' unanswered; unclaimed-bev 'what will you open' unanswered; travel-bev asked about disability; credit-aisha asked for card digits with no reason
suggested_acceptance: Interview prompt answers any question in the person's text first; LC detector shows 0 unanswered questions

title: Chores built on one state's law are offered to everyone with no residency gate
expected: A residency precondition is asked first, and the rule set adapts or the chore says it does not apply
got: data-broker = California Delete Act/DROP (Bev in Virginia, brief still adds her maiden name to the California request); subscription = California Automatic Renewal Law (Aisha AZ, Bev VA); unclaimed = RUUPA as IL/VT enacted it, run for OH/VA (offline: neither enacted RUUPA)
suggested_acceptance: Each state-law playbook declares a jurisdiction; adopt asks residency and the brief states which law applies

title: data-broker shows '$0 a year' and 'Worth $0 a year', honest but it reads as worthless
expected: Value in its real unit: ~12 hours a year, or a $129/yr removal service avoided
got: Catalogue and topic show $0; basis has 180 min x 4 and DeleteMe $129

expected: Values compared on a stated common unit
got: 5 of 11 consumer chores are per episode; eu261 $1,300/episode ranks above credit $1,000/yr
